finding.expected: Keep the existing source-product-id parser as the item-id authority, but add a fail-closed direct-product-route proof around it: the normalized current/target host must be an accepted Shopee host and the current PATH itself must match one of the supported direct product route shapes (-i.{shop_id}.{item_id}, exact /product/{shop_id}/{item_id}, or exact /item/{item_id}) rather than merely containing one of those substrings. Any search/unrelated/verification/challenge path, including one that embeds a target-looking product token, must perform exactly one navigation to the requested target URL. Add focused regressions for those same-host false-positive path shapes while preserving the K550 zero-navigation continuity case, TASK-162 readiness, selected-variant evidence semantics, and the 0-or-1 navigation invariant.
finding.issue: TASK-175 requires zero-navigation reuse only when the acquired current page is deterministically proven to be the exact direct Shopee product target; search and unrelated Shopee pages must remain unproven and perform one target navigation. The new _can_reuse_current_page(...) predicate does not prove that direct-route shape. After host equality and a small verify/challenge/captcha segment exclusion, it calls extract_shopee_product_id(current.path) and accepts any matching item id. That existing parser intentionally uses unanchored re.search patterns, so an unrelated/search path that merely embeds a recognized token such as /search/foo-i.123.456789 or another non-product path containing /product/123/456789 can falsely authorize reuse. The predicate also proves only current_host == target_host; it never proves that the matching host is actually the Shopee product host required by the TASK. Current regressions cover a normal /search URL with the id only in query state, but not an unrelated same-host path containing a recognized product-id pattern, so this false positive remains untested. In that state the extractor can skip the required target navigation and evaluate a non-product DOM while claiming same-target continuity.
